question_en: What are the manufacturer and model of the instrument in the image?
gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · P2-2-2-F02

## Step 01 · Record the dual plate stage and optical head, search for a photogrammetric instrument photo

**Action:** Extract from the current image the yellow long crossbeam, tilted binocular observation head, two rectangular photo stages placed side by side, left and right marking heads, and illumination components. Search terms could be "photogrammetry comparator point transfer instrument yellow binocular".

**Evidence Observation:** The dual-stage structure suggests a comparator or point-transfer type photogrammetric instrument, but several models from the same manufacturer have very similar appearances; the blurred area with a person does not participate in model identification, nor can one assume a hidden coordinate encoder configuration from the image.

## Step 02 · Locate the original photo and clear caption in university lecture notes

**Action:** Consult Aalto's photogrammetry lecture notes, locate the photo at the bottom of page 12 of the PDF, then read the caption below it to avoid misreading the model of the figure at the top of the same page.

Lecture PDF:
http://foto.aalto.fi/opetus/301/luennot/301_2_2004.pdf

**Evidence Observation:** The lower figure on page 12 corresponds to the input image in terms of binocular head tilt angle, yellow crossbeam, and the layout of left and right stages with marking heads; the caption states "Monokomparaattori ja ylivientikoje Kern CPM1". The upper part of the same page shows a Zeiss PSK2, which does not belong to the lower photo in this problem. The top of page 13 continues to provide CPM1 details, while the Zeiss PM1 at the bottom is another device.

**Result of this step:** The matching photo and explicit caption have tied the target to Kern CPM1; this binding is more direct than guessing the brand based on the yellow casing.

## Step 03 · Verify with the original manufacturer brochure, handle strong confusion with PMG2

**Action:** Compare the whole instrument on page 2 and the stage and marking heads on page 3 of the Kern CPM1 original brochure PDF, then read the technical paper by Kern engineer Klaver regarding the relationship between PMG2 and CPM1.

CPM1 Original Brochure:
https://www.kern-aarau.ch/fileadmin/user_upload/Aldo/Prospekte_Photo/1980-04-01_14Ee_Kern_CPM1_Comparator_Point_Marker.pdf

Technical Paper (relevant explanations on PDF pages 1 and 3):
https://www.isprs.org/proceedings/XXIII/congress/part9/260_XXIII-B9.pdf

**Evidence Observation:** The whole instrument in the original brochure matches the dual plate stage, binocular head, and marking device; the technical literature explains that CPM1 is based on PMG2 with added coordinate measurement configuration. Therefore, PMG2 is a strong neighbor; one cannot claim to completely exclude it based solely on the front yellow casing, nor can one treat encoders not clearly shown in the problem image as observed differences. The final model is still determined jointly by the original photo caption and CPM1 documents.

PMG2 Original Brochure:
https://www.kern-aarau.ch/fileadmin/user_upload/Aldo/Prospekte_Photo/1980-05-01_204e_Kern_PMG2_Point_Transfer_and_Marking_Instrument.pdf

The MK2 original brochure shows a single-stage, monocular layout; the Zeiss PM1 in the lecture notes has a different rear vertical optical structure and front panel, which can serve as a more distant visual comparison:
https://www.kern-aarau.ch/fileadmin/user_upload/Aldo/Prospekte_Photo/1973-07-01_211e_Kern_MK2_Monocomparator.pdf

ER2 in the CPM1 brochure is the name of a matching recording device and cannot be taken as the main model in the problem image.

## Step 04 · Stop after confirming manufacturer and model

**Action:** Re-check the archive names for CPM1, PMG2, and MK2 from the Kern product archive entry; the page is used to locate the original brochure, not as a new photo match.

Corresponding product archives:
https://www.kern-aarau.ch/kern-extern/produkte-c.html

https://www.kern-aarau.ch/kern-extern/produkte-p.html

https://www.kern-aarau.ch/kern-extern/produkte-m.html

**Stopping Condition:** Both the image caption and original manufacturer documents support manufacturer Kern and model CPM1; the problem does not require instrument principles, measurement accuracy, or matching recorders, so directly outputting the two items is sufficient.

## Formal Answer

Kern；CPM1
